questions.q: The correct sequence of steps in a single machine cycle is:
questions.solution: The CPU first Fetches the instruction from memory, Decodes it in the control unit, Executes it in the ALU, and Stores the result.
questions.shortcut: Fat Dogs Eat Snacks: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store. Any option starting with Decode/Execute is out.

questions.q: Which shortcut **pastes** copied content?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+V** pastes; Ctrl+X cuts, Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+P prints.

questions.q: Which extension stores plain text with NO formatting at all?
questions.solution: **.txt** keeps only characters — no bold, fonts, colours or images. .rtf keeps simple formatting, .odt and .docx keep full formatting.

questions.q: Which shortcut opens the **browser history** page?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+H = History** in Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: The fixed phrase is **in spite of** repeated warnings = although they were warned many times. *Due of* does not exist (*due to* has no 'of'); 'fined instead of repeated warnings' and 'ahead of repeated warnings' make no sense — the sentence concedes the warnings and still imposes the fine.
questions.shortcut: '___ of' + a concession meaning → in spite of.
questions.passage: Every June the municipal office on the fourth floor turns into a monsoon war room. The control room answers complaints round the clock (1) ______ the monsoon, and staff keep sandbags ready for the low-lying ward. The executive engineer insists that drains must be desilted (2) ______ the first showers arrive, not after them. Contractors who delay the work are fined (3) ______ of repeated warnings. Residents can now report a blocked drain by phone, and the office responds (4) ______ every complaint within a day.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

They said, "Hurrah! We have won the trophy."
options: They said with joy that they have won the trophy.
They exclaimed with joy that they would win the trophy.
They exclaimed with joy that they had won the trophy.
They exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the trophy.
questions.solution: Hurrah → **exclaimed with joy**; present perfect → past perfect; we → they. B inverts the tone; C keeps the un-shifted 'have won'; D changes the tense to would.
questions.shortcut: Hurrah = joy, Alas = sorrow; then backshift the tense.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Neither of the two ministers **were present** at the cabinet meeting.
questions.solution: **Neither** is singular; *ministers* sits inside the 'of' phrase → neither **was present**. 'Were being' repeats the plural fault, and 'has been present' breaks the simple-past narration.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: The doctor repeats the passage's controlling metaphor: a market **sells** — and this one sells food but really 'sells company'. *Paints*, *measures* and *imports* are grammatical verbs, but each breaks the selling idea the whole passage runs on. Reading the passage first tells you the writer is still inside the market metaphor.
questions.shortcut: Theme check: the sentence plays on 'market → selling'; keep the verb that stays inside the metaphor.
questions.passage: When the textile mill in Erode added a night shift, hundreds of workers finished duty at two in the morning — and found every shop shut. Within months, a small night market appeared near the mill gate: tea stalls, a barber, a pharmacy and carts selling hot (1) ______. Traders say trust is their main (2) ______: goods are left on open shelves, and payments are dropped into a tin, yet nothing is ever missing. A doctor who volunteers at the market's first-aid desk notes that many workers come not to buy but to talk. 'The market sells food, but what it really (3) ______ is company,' he says. The corporation, which once fined the traders for blocking the road, has now built them a covered (4) ______ with lights and a water tap.

questions.q: The most abundant **metal in the human body** is —
questions.solution: **Calcium** (bones and teeth) tops the body's metal list; iron is the most abundant trace metal. Oxygen is the most abundant element overall.

questions.q: Who was the **first woman Governor** of an Indian state?
questions.solution: **Sarojini Naidu** became Governor of the United Provinces (now UP) in 1947. Sucheta Kriplani was the first woman Chief Minister (UP, 1963). Her daughter Padmaja Naidu later governed West Bengal.

questions.q: The stated purpose of the **Partition of Bengal (1905)** was —
questions.solution: Curzon claimed the province was too big to govern; nationalists saw the real aim — splitting Bengali unity — and launched the Swadeshi movement.
questions.shortcut: Stated = administrative; real = divide the nationalists.

questions.q: The Sangam-age Chera king associated with the **Kannagi (Pattini) cult** is —
questions.solution: **Senguttuvan** (the 'red Chera') is credited with instituting the **Pattini cult** of the chaste heroine Kannagi, as described in the *Silappadikaram*'s later tradition.

questions.q: A can do $\frac{2}{5}$ of a work in 6 days and B can do $\frac{3}{4}$ of the same work in 9 days. Working together, they complete the work in:
questions.solution:
A: full work in $\frac{6 \times 5}{2} = 15$ days; B: $\frac{9 \times 4}{3} = 12$ days.
Together: $\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3}{20}$ ⇒ $6\frac{2}{3}$ days.
questions.shortcut: Scale each to full-work time first (15 and 12), then combine.

questions.q: A triangle with sides $3$ cm, $4$ cm and $5$ cm is similar to a larger triangle whose longest side is $20$ cm. The perimeter of the larger triangle is:
questions.solution:
$k = \frac{20}{5} = 4$; sides become $12, 16, 20$.

Perimeter $= 4 \times 12 = 48$ cm.
questions.shortcut: Perimeter scales by $k = 4$: $12 \times 4 = 48$ cm. Trap: $60$ ($5 \times 12$, mixing sides).

questions.q: The shadow of a pole is $\sqrt{3}$ times the height of the pole. The angle of elevation of the sun is:
questions.solution: $\tan\theta=\frac{h}{\sqrt3\,h}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\Rightarrow\theta=30^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: Shadow $\sqrt3\times$ height is the signature of 30° ($d=\sqrt3h$). Trap: 60° inverts the ratio.

questions.q: A tumbler is a frustum of a cone with radii $4$ cm and $2$ cm and height $21$ cm. Its volume is (take $\pi = 22/7$):
questions.solution: $16 + 4 + 8 = 28$; $V = \frac13 \times 21 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 28 = 7 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 28 = 616$ cu cm.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Dengue cases in the city have risen sharply this month.

**Courses of action:**
I. The civic body should clear stagnant water where mosquitoes breed.
II. Government hospitals should set up special fever counters.

Which of the courses of action follow(s)?
options: Only course of action II follows
Only course of action I follows
questions.solution: I attacks the cause (breeding sites) — **follows**. II gives relief to those already ill — **follows**. Prevention and relief do not cancel each other. Answer: **both**.

questions.q: **X is older than Y. Z is younger than W. V is older than X. W is older than V. Y is older than Z.** Who is the **third oldest**?
questions.solution: Chain: W > V > X > Y > Z (W is pinned above V; V above X; X above Y; Y above Z; and Z < W is automatic). Third oldest = **X**.
questions.shortcut: Build the spine W > V > X, then hang Y and Z below X.

questions.q: Select the related number: **25 : 49 :: 34 : ?**
questions.solution: Digit sum of 25 is 2+5 = 7 and 7² = 49. Digit sum of 34 is 3+4 = 7, and 7² = **49**. Both members share digit sum 7 — the answer is its square again.
questions.shortcut: When a and b look unrelated, compute the digit sum: many CGL analogies are (digit sum)² or (digit sum)×k.

questions.q: **In a class of 60 students, Neha ranks 23rd from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?**
questions.solution: $60 - 23 + 1$ = **38th** from the bottom.
